title: Post-pandemic growth returns for PC and console, driven by premium spending and changing price dynamics | Newzoo
text:
Emmanuel RosierDirector of Market Intelligence

March 12, 2026

Premium spending is rising in Western markets and the $30–$ 50 tier is emerging as the fastest-growing price band.

The global PC and console games market is projected to reach $103.7 billion by 2028, according to Newzoo's PC & Console Gaming Report 2026, marking the end of the post-pandemic revenue plateau.

2025 was the first year of notable revenue growth in the industry since the pandemic, increasing 7% year-over-year. This marks the beginning of what appears to be a new cycle of consolidated nominal expansion through 2028.

Newzoo forecasts PC revenue to grow at a 6.6% CAGR between 2025 and 2028, compared with 4.4% for console, with PC projected to surpass console revenue by 2028.

## The market is picking up, but the two platforms have different business propositions and contexts

"Growth is returning to the market, but it's being driven by different fundamentals than during the pandemic years," said Manu Rosier, Director of Market Intelligence at Newzoo. "Hardware cycles are stretching, development costs are rising, and even proven franchises are no longer guaranteed to succeed. The rules that shaped the industry over the past two decades are changing. PC and console ecosystems are evolving in different directions."

### PC: player base is increasing, business models evolve, and more competition arises below entrenched leaders

PC expansion continues to be driven by global player scale.

- The PC player base is projected to exceed one billion players by 2028 and regional momentum is a key factor: China grew 11.7% YoY in 2025. We also expect continued growth tied to expanding PC ecosystem penetration and storefront adoption.
- PC monetization remains structurally microtransaction-led. In 2025, microtransactions accounted for 48% of PC revenue ($20.6B)**, while **premium game sales represented 29% ($ 12.5B).
- Premium games were the main PC growth driver in 2025 (+11.8% YoY), supported by a dense slate of premium releases across AAA, AA, and indie segments, many in the $30-$ 50 price range.
- In major Western markets, PC free-to-play revenue per playing hour increased 10% year-on-year, reaching nearly 2× PlayStation and 3× Xbox.
- Engagement is becoming more distributed. Between 2022 and 2025, the share of PC playtime generated by games outside the Top 20 titles increased from 33% to 42%, reflecting growing ecosystem breadth beyond the largest franchises.

### Console: slower player base growth, premium-led growth and higher revenue per player, more concentrated around blockbuster releases and hardware cycles

- Console revenue and player base are expected to grow, but at a slower pace than PC.
- Mature markets such as North America and Japan continue to generate higher spend per player.
- Engagement and revenue are also more concentrated on console. In 2025, premium games accounted for roughly half of console revenues and grew by ~12% year-over-year, supported by major franchise releases and annualized titles.
- Console microtransaction revenues declined slightly, reflecting weaker spending across several live-service ecosystems.
- Subscription revenues continued to grow modestly, though growth is increasingly driven by price increases and tier upgrades rather than expanding subscriber bases.
- Free-to-play revenues declined faster than playtime in 2025.
- Titles priced above $50 still represent nearly 80% of total premium revenues on console, though lower-priced titles are gaining traction across platforms.
- PlayStation remains more hit-driven, with engagement concentrated among the Top 20 and annual franchises.
- On Xbox, engagement is spreading beyond the Top 20, partly driven by discovery through Game Pass. Though this reflects redistribution of playtime rather than overall engagement growth.

## Premium spending drives growth in Western markets

Across major Western markets, including the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, France, Spain, and Italy, Newzoo data shows premium spending increased in 2025 even as playtime declined.

PC — Premium revenue on PC in our selected markets grew by 17.4% YoY.

- Battlefield 6 was by far the most important contributor, with notable performance from ARC Raiders and a large slate of other premium single-player games.
- Both Battlefield and ARC Raiders have a PC skew compared to CoD's console skew.
- The PC audience seems to be increasingly accustomed to premium single-player games.

PlayStation – Premium grows, while Free-to-play contracts.

To explain 2025's performance, it's helpful to look at previous years.

- Annual sports titles saw a sizable increase in 2023, with Hogwarts Legacy and Marvel's Spider-Man 2 contributing as well.
- In 2024, Fortnite had an amazing year, particularly after the launch of OG. We also had the first full year of Roblox on consoles, as well as an impressive slate of major title releases: EA College Football, HELLDIVERS 2, Dragon Ball Sparking Zero, Black Myth: Wukong, and many more.
- Even though 2025 was impressive and premium grew by 7.8%, revenue slips from CoD and Fortnite were noticeable. Destiny 2, Apex Legends, and Rainbow Six Siege X all suffered contraction.
- Even the very impressive Roblox growth and continued success of PS+ subscription (particularly the higher tiers) couldn't offset those losses.

Xbox — Xbox is more challenged than PS across all monetization types. Single-player titles see lower engagement, partly because Game Pass altered expectations on the platform.

Now let's take a look at how games from different price points performed over the past few years.

### The $30–$ 50 price band is emerging as the fastest-growing tier across platforms.

This mid-price segment is expanding as players experiment with finding the best cost/fun ratio between indie pricing and $70 releases.

- ARC Raiders stands out as a huge success across all platforms. It follows in the footsteps of HELLDIVERS 2, which launched on Xbox this year to incredible success once more.
- This price range could be utilized by many upcoming multiplayer games, remakes/remasters, and AA games such as Mafia. Increasing the price at the high end created opportunities here to offer great value to players without committing to the full price.

### Sub-$30 titles are capturing a larger share of PC spending

The number of games priced below $30 generating more than **$ 5 million in revenue increased from 17 in 2024 to 26 in 2025**, reflecting the commercial impact of breakout titles and viral indie hits.

- New games tend to perform better on PC, since the platform's audience is more dynamic in its preferences.
- Even though console represents a smaller share of the market, titles like Dispatch and REMATCH still benefited significantly from their console versions. A game's core design often determines whether it fits PC, console, or both better.
- Schedule I has higher revenue than Minecraft in our scope on PC. Its launch in March, an emptier part of the year, accounted for a large proportion of its very significant revenue. This shows that, under the right circumstances, the premium revenue potential of sub-$30 games is very high on PC. It is a hard space to get into, with significant competition, but 2025 showed that even low budget hits can reach the top of the revenue rankings.
- Minecraft still gets significant premium revenue, although the recurring revenue accounts for a larger share on consoles - especially on Xbox, likely because of Game Pass.

### The $50+ segment remains console-led but is flattening on Xbox

PlayStation recorded 81 titles surpassing $5M revenue in 2025, while Xbox recorded 34, reflecting weaker premium momentum.

- Despite being heavily concentrated at the top, with EA Sports FC and NBA 2K dominating, PlayStation still recorded 81 games earning over $5M in 2025, the same number as PC. The difference is that PlayStation wins through the sheer size of the segment, while PC achieves the same breadth through a more diverse player base.
- Annual sports titles dominate console top charts. Xbox remains meaningful but accounts for an increasingly smaller share, with only 34 titles crossing the $5M threshold.
- Since annual sports aren't so dominant on PC, there are more opportunities for different titles to claim market share.

"With engagement stabilizing, premium performance and pricing strategy are increasingly determining where revenue growth occurs," continues Rosier. "Scale alone no longer guarantees outcomes. Understanding where players are spending time, and why, has become strategic imperative."
